claim: Tone is the single tonality word every department reads when nothing more specific is set, and it lands mostly on the face and the colour temperature. You reach for it when the scene content is neutral but the feeling must not be — the same boy on the same pitch is a different film at earnest versus savage.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: earnest expression, direct clear gaze, even warm light
wistful, distant gaze, soft hazy light, faded warmth
melancholy, downcast eyes, muted blue palette
tender expression, gentle half-smile, soft warm glow
tense, clenched jaw, hard-edged shadows, cold contrast
dread, wide fearful eyes, creeping shadow, desaturated cold
playful, grin, bright cheerful light, light-hearted
comedic, exaggerated open-mouth expression, bright flat light
cold expression, flat stare, cool desaturated palette, distant
bittersweet, sad smile, wet eyes, warm light cool shadow
triumphant, exultant expression, radiant backlight, blazing
eerie, unsettling stillness, pale sickly glow, blank stare
serene, calm expression, soft diffuse light, tranquil
savage, feral grin, bared teeth, harsh raking light

review.issue: absurd ("absurd, surreal, nonsensical, deadpan bizarre") is three non-tags plus "surreal". Only "surreal" carries weight, so the panel will land close to the neutral control and teach nothing about the option.
review.fix: Anchor it in something drawable that is not subject-restating: "surreal, deadpan expression, incongruous object, dreamlike composition".
